title: Treewidth classification of approximate counting CSP
formal: Assume that parameterized Clique has no randomized fixed-parameter algorithm with bounded error. For every fixed recursively enumerable class C of finite relational structures with a uniform bound on relation arity, are the following equivalent: (1) counting homomorphisms \(A\to B\) for \(A\in C\) and arbitrary compatible B is exactly solvable in polynomial time; (2) this problem admits a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme; (3) it admits a fixed-parameter randomized approximation scheme with parameter \(\Vert A\Vert\); and (4) the Gaifman graphs of structures in C have bounded treewidth? The missing implication is \((3)\Rightarrow (4)\). No fan-grid containment, minor closure or other closure property is assumed for C. This is the source’s Theorem 3 with its fan-class hypothesis removed.
context:
Bounded treewidth gives exact polynomial-time counting, which yields an FPRAS and then an FPTRAS. The source proves the converse under its additional fan-class hypothesis; its conclusion asks whether that hypothesis can be removed.

The journal discusses the exact-counting classification by treewidth of the structures themselves. Decision can instead depend on treewidth modulo homomorphic equivalence. Replacing raw treewidth by core treewidth would change this approximation question.

Theorem 3.2 keeps the fan-class condition, including the minor-closed cases, and Section 5 repeats the question for all bounded-arity classes. The indexing change from conference Theorem 3 does not signal a broader theorem.

The 2024 list-homomorphism article gives exact running-time bases for each fixed target graph H, using treewidth of the source graph as a parameter. Here C restricts the source structures and the entire target structure B is unrestricted input.
why: Would determine whether approximation enlarges the tractable classes of structurally restricted counting CSPs, and whether treewidth remains the complete structural criterion.

definitions: A finite relational signature \(\tau\) is a finite collection of relation symbols, each with a specified nonnegative integer arity. A finite \(\tau\)-structure A consists of a finite universe \(V(A)\) and, for every r-ary \(R\in \tau , a\) set \(R^{A}\subseteq V(A)\)ʳ. Input structures A and B share \(\tau\), but \(\tau\) may vary between instances. Every arity is at most a constant \(r_{C}\) fixed for the class C. Universes, symbols, arities and relation tuples are explicitly listed in a standard binary encoding; \(\Vert A\Vert\) denotes its length, and similarly for B. Nullary relations, if present, are either empty or contain the empty tuple and are checked in the same way as other relations. A homomorphism is any function \(h:V(A)\to V(B)\) such that for each relation tuple \((a_{1},\ldots ,a_{r})\in R^{A}\), the tuple \((h(a_{1}),\ldots ,h(a_{r}))\) belongs to \(R^{B}\). It need not be injective or surjective. Count all such functions, including zero when none exists. C is fixed before the input and can be enumerated by a Turing machine; a promised input has \(A\in C\), and an algorithm need not decide membership in C. The Gaifman graph \(G(A)\) has universe \(V(A)\) as vertices and joins distinct elements occurring together in some relation tuple. A tree decomposition assigns vertex bags to a tree so that every vertex is in a bag, every edge has both ends in a bag, and bags containing a given vertex form a connected subtree. Its width is the largest bag size minus one; treewidth is the minimum width, with empty graph assigned width zero here. Bounded treewidth of C means one constant w works for every \(A\in C\). It refers to A itself, not to a homomorphically equivalent core. An approximation scheme receives A,B and a rational \(0<\varepsilon <1\) and outputs an integer random variable X satisfying \(\Pr [|X- H|\le \varepsilon H]\ge 3/4\), where H is the homomorphism count. In particular it must output zero with that probability when \(H=0\). Probability is over internal fair random bits. An FPRAS uses time polynomial in \(\Vert A\Vert +\Vert B\Vert +\varepsilon ^{- 1}\); an FPTRAS uses \(f(\Vert A\Vert )\cdot (\Vert A\Vert +\Vert B\Vert +\varepsilon ^{- 1})^{a}\) for a computable f and constant a. Reading the rational accuracy encoding is included. These are worst-case time bounds, and a,f and the algorithm may depend on fixed C but not on individual input structures. The hypothesis means that no uniform randomized algorithm decides whether an N-vertex graph has a k-clique in \(g(k)N^{b}\) time for computable g and constant b, with error at most \(1/4\) on every instance. This states explicitly the randomized parameterized separation used in the source.
answer_criterion: Under the stated parameterized complexity hypothesis, prove the equivalence for every eligible class C, or refute it by a recursively enumerable bounded-arity class of unbounded Gaifman treewidth with an FPTRAS for its homomorphism-counting problem. The other implications are already known. An exact-counting hardness result, a theorem only for minor-closed or fan classes, or a classification with the right-hand structure fixed does not establish the missing unrestricted implication.
